claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based plasma-facing materials are governed by the extent of grain-boundary impurity segregation, particularly oxygen segregation.
Grain-boundary oxygen segregation alters grain-boundary diffusivity.
Grain-boundary oxygen segregation alters grain-boundary cohesion.
A controlled low-level increase in grain-boundary oxygen segregation promotes dynamic grain-boundary relaxation.
Oxygen atoms segregated at tungsten grain boundaries reduce the activation energy for dislocation climb.
Grain-boundary oxygen promotes dislocation climb by increasing local diffusivity.
Grain-boundary oxygen promotes grain-boundary sliding by increasing local diffusivity.
Oxygen-enabled dynamic recovery relieves stress concentrations at grain boundaries during high-temperature deformation.
Relieving grain-boundary stress concentrations delays crack initiation and propagation.
Oxygen-lean grain boundaries are more resistant to diffusion-assisted deformation processes.
Resistance to diffusion-assisted deformation at oxygen-lean boundaries causes earlier strain localization and lower toughness.
Low-level oxygen-enriched specimens will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure than specimens with negligible grain-boundary oxygen.
Low-level oxygen-enriched specimens will exhibit higher high-temperature fracture toughness than the baseline material.
High-temperature tensile load-displacement behavior will show increased ductility and delayed strain localization after grain-boundary oxygen enrichment.
The proposed effect applies above approximately 1200 °C, where diffusion-enabled deformation mechanisms are active.
The proposed mechanism may not operate at lower temperatures because atomic mobility is insufficient.
The beneficial effect occurs only within a narrow oxygen-doping window.
Excessive oxygen can embrittle tungsten-based plasma-facing materials.
